title: Excessive time spent online linked to stress and worse mood – study
excerpt: German study surveyed adults who engage in gaming, pornography and online shopping
content_html:
Spending excessive time online is associated with higher stress levels, worse mood, and greater neglect of other activities, according to analysis.

The new study by academics at the University of Duisburg-Essen published in the journal PLOS One, surveyed 900 German adults in 2025 who reported engaging in gaming, pornography use, social network use, or online shopping at least once in the last year.

Depending on the frequency of their usage, their internet use was labelled as either pathological, risky, or non-problematic. Problematic internet usage, which includes pathological and risky usage, was defined by the study as the excessive use of online applications to the point of functional impairment or distress.

The study’s participants then completed an assessment every evening for two weeks, where they reported their mood and stress levels, temptation to engage in problematic internet use, and their total time spent on the internet more generally. The assessment also measured how much pleasure was derived from internet usage and whether any other activities were neglected as a result.

Participants with more severe problematic internet usage were associated with worse mood, more stress, longer internet use times and greater neglect of other areas of life. The study also found that temptation was the main driver for continued internet use, with feelings of pleasure and relief emerging as reinforcing factors.

Andreas Oelker, co-author of the study, said: “More than actual stress or mood alone, it is the momentary urge to go online that determines whether people engage in online activities and experience both rewarding and harmful consequences.

“Understanding why individuals at risk of problematic internet use go online at particular moments is essential for developing better prevention and treatment strategies. Our findings suggest that helping people recognise and manage moments of temptation may be more effective than focusing on stress or mood alone.”

The study’s results confirmed the researchers’ hypothesis that daily stress, mood and temptation could be used to predict a person’s daily internet usage, and further, how these factors in turn affect daily pleasure, relief and neglect of other activities. Researchers stress that not all types of internet usage have negative outcomes, but rather problematic or excessive usage.

Silke M. Müller, co-author of the study, said: “We’d like to note that only a small percentage of internet users develop pathological use patterns. Using the internet brings joy, fun, and/or relief from stress in an enriching way as long as other important areas of life are not systematically neglected.

“These areas include not only essential duties and responsibilities, but also other activities that have been proven to have a positive effect on our wellbeing and health, such as exercise, spending time outdoors, or doing things with friends.”

Previous studies have suggested that young people with internet addiction experience changes in their brain chemistry which could lead to more addictive behaviours, and that these effects were evident throughout multiple neural networks in the brain alongside increased activity in parts of the brain when participants were resting.

content_html_zh:
分析显示，上网时间过长会带来更高的压力、更糟糕的情绪以及更容易忽视其他活动。

杜伊斯堡-埃森大学学者在《PLOS One》杂志上发表的这项新研究对 2025 年的 900 名德国成年人进行了调查，他们表示在过去一年中至少参与过一次游戏、色情内容、社交网络或网上购物。

根据他们的使用频率，他们的互联网使用被标记为病态、有风险或无问题。 该研究将有问题的互联网使用（包括病态和危险使用）定义为过度使用在线应用程序以致功能受损或痛苦。

然后，该研究的参与者在两周内每天晚上完成一项评估，报告他们的情绪和压力水平、有问题的互联网使用的诱惑，以及他们在互联网上花费的总时间。 该评估还衡量了从使用互联网中获得的快乐程度以及是否因此而忽略了任何其他活动。

互联网使用问题更严重的参与者情绪更差、压力更大、互联网使用时间更长以及对生活其他领域的忽视程度更高。 研究还发现，诱惑是持续使用互联网的主要驱动力，而愉悦感和轻松感则是强化因素。

该研究的合著者安德烈亚斯·奥尔克（Andreas Oelker）表示：“不仅仅是实际的压力或情绪，上网的短暂冲动决定了人们是否参与在线活动并经历有益和有害的后果。

“了解面临互联网使用问题风险的个人为何在特定时刻上网对于制定更好的预防和治疗策略至关重要。 我们的研究结果表明，帮助人们识别和管理诱惑的时刻可能比单独关注压力或情绪更有效。”

该研究的结果证实了研究人员的假设，即日常压力、情绪和诱惑可以用来预测一个人的日常互联网使用情况，以及这些因素反过来如何影响日常愉悦、缓解和忽视其他活动。 研究人员强调，并非所有类型的互联网使用都会产生负面结果，而是会产生问题或过度使用。

西尔克·M. 该研究的合著者穆勒表示：“我们想指出，只有一小部分互联网用户形成了病态的使用模式。 只要生活的其他重要领域不被系统性地忽视，使用互联网就会以一种丰富的方式带来欢乐、乐趣和/或缓解压力。

“这些领域不仅包括基本的职责和责任，还包括其他已被证明对我们的福祉和健康产生积极影响的活动，例如锻炼、户外活动或与朋友一起做事。”

先前的研究表明，患有网络成瘾的年轻人的大脑化学物质会发生变化，这可能会导致更多的成瘾行为，而且这些影响在大脑中的多个神经网络中都很明显，而且当参与者休息时，大脑部分区域的活动也会增加。
